content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Los Alamos

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: The PMP® credential requires either a four-year degree plus three years of project-management experience, or a high school diploma plus five years of equivalent experience. Review PMI's full eligibility criteria to ensure you meet education and hours logged before applying.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP® training course. Attend all scheduled sessions from your Los Alamos location—no travel required. Our active certified practitioners guide you through core frameworks, real-world application, and exam readiness over the full course term.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing your training hours, submit your PMP® application directly to PMI, including documentation of your project-management experience and education. Pay the PMI examination fee when you apply. Our course team can answer questions about the submission process.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Sit for the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources—practice tests, study guides, and office hours—to solidify your knowledge. Schedule your exam at a Pearson VUE testing center. You may test in-person or at home, depending on your preference and PMI regulations.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP® Credential
steps_items.text: After certification, earn professional development units (PDUs) over a three-year renewal cycle to keep your credential active. PMI offers multiple pathways to earn PDUs through training, volunteering, and on-the-job practice. Renew before your expiration date to remain certified.
